types.label: Event
types.description: Something that happens at a time, such as a meeting, a flight or a birthday.

description.description: A short description of the event.

starts_at.label: Starts
starts_at.description: When the event starts, as an ISO 8601 instant. `timezone` says which local time it means.

ends_at.label: Ends
ends_at.description: When the event ends, as an ISO 8601 instant.

duration.description: How long the event lasts, in seconds. For a repeating event with no `ends_at`, it is the length of each occurrence.

place.description: Where the event happens, as a name or an address.

url.label: URL
url.description: A web page about the event.

precision.description: How much of the start is known, such as only the year, for an event dated from memory.

notes.description: Your own comments, kept apart from the event's details.

recurrence.description: RFC 5545 recurrence lines (RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE) that make the event repeat. Marfa works out the occurrences when they are read instead of storing them.

all_day.description: True when the event lasts whole days rather than a span of time. Read the date from `starts_at` in the event's `timezone`.

timezone.label: Time Zone
timezone.description: The IANA time zone the event keeps its local hour in, such as Europe/Berlin. A repeating event keeps that hour across daylight saving changes.

end_timezone.label: End Time Zone
end_timezone.description: The IANA time zone the event ends in, when it differs from `timezone`, such as a flight that lands in another zone.

attendees.description: The people invited, one entry each. An entry has a name, an email or both, and the person's reply.

name.description: The attendee's name as the source gives it

response.description: The attendee's reply to the invitation

original_starts_at.label: Original Start
original_starts_at.description: For an event that replaces one occurrence of a repeating event, the start of the occurrence it replaces.

executable.description: Whether the file may be run as a program. Absent means it may not.

size_bytes.label: Size

types.label: Message

types.description: A table you keep by hand, such as a budget, a reading log or a list of contacts, with the columns you choose.

types.label: Task

description.description: A line or two of context.

body.description: The full details, as long as you need.

starts_at.label: Starts

precision.description: How much of the task's date is known, such as only the year or the month.

url.label: URL
url.description: A web page related to the task.

assignees.description: The people the task is assigned to, one entry each. An entry has a name, an email or both.

name.description: The assignee's name as the source gives it, such as a login

notes.description: Your own comments, kept apart from the task's details.

recurrence.description: RFC 5545 recurrence lines (RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE) that make the task repeat, counted from `due_at` or, without one, from `starts_at`.

types.label: Connection
types.description: An app you signed in to Marfa, with the access you gave it and when it last used it.

name.description: Your own name for this app's sign-in. Without one, the app's registered name is used.

scopes.description: The scopes you granted the app.

status.description: Whether the sign-in is active or revoked.

last_used_at.description: When the app last used the sign-in successfully.

revoked_at.description: When you revoked the sign-in, if you did.

types.label: Folder
types.description: A folder kept in sync with Marfa, with which items it holds and how new files are filed, shared by every machine that uses it.

query.description: Which items the folder holds, chosen by type, tier, state, a filter or a position under an item.

defaults.description: What a new file gets where its frontmatter leaves a blank: type, tier, properties, tags and edges. It is never applied to an edited file.

include.description: Paths the folder takes, as gitignore patterns relative to its root. Empty takes every path.

ignore.description: Paths the folder leaves alone, as gitignore patterns relative to its root. It wins over `include`.

first_placement.description: Where a new item of a type made elsewhere first appears: a map from type to a directory under the folder's root.

removal_threshold.description: When removing files pauses for confirmation: more than `files` files and more than `fraction` of the folder at once. Defaults to 10 and 0.25.

full_pass_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the watch's passes that read every file in the folder, from 60 to 86400. Defaults to 600.

addition_threshold.description: When new files pause for confirmation: a scan that would add more than `files` files and more than `fraction` of the folder's files. Defaults to 50 and 0.25.

outside_query.description: What the folder does with a new file its query would not hold: send it and keep it flagged unmatched, or hold it on disk, not sent. Defaults to send.

types.label: View
types.description: A saved list of items, with the order and grouping you chose, shared by every app.

query.description: Which items the view lists, chosen by type, tier, state, a filter or a position under an item.

sort.description: The keys the view sorts by, first key first. Each has a `by` field and a `direction`, `asc` or `desc`.

group.description: How the view groups its items: by a field or an edge, optionally in day, week, month or year buckets, with the group order and any hidden groups.

edge_types.label: About
edge_types.description: Says that an item is about another item, such as a note about a book.

edge_types.label: Attached to
edge_types.description: Says that an item is attached to another item and exists for it, such as a scanned page attached to the document it was scanned for.

position.description: Where the attachment comes among the item's attachments, such as the page number of a scan.

edge_types.label: Comment on
edge_types.description: Says that an item is a comment on another item, including a reply to another comment.

edge_types.label: Derived from
edge_types.description: Says that an item was made from another item, such as an imported copy or a summary generated from a note.

edge_types.label: Excerpt from
edge_types.description: Says that an item is a highlight, quote or clip taken from another item, such as a quote from a book.

edge_types.label: In collection
edge_types.description: Says that an item is a member of a container, such as a collection, a series or an album.

position.description: Where the item comes among the container's members.

edge_types.label: In folder
edge_types.description: Says where an item's file sits in a synced folder.

path.description: The file's path from the folder's root.

edge_types.label: In thread
edge_types.description: Says that an item is a message in a thread, such as a reply in a conversation.

position.description: Where the message comes in the thread.

edge_types.label: Children
edge_types.description: Says that an item is the parent of another item, so that items form a hierarchy.

edge_types.label: References
edge_types.description: Says that an item mentions another item, such as a note that links to another note.

edge_types.label: Supersedes
edge_types.description: Says that an item replaces another item as the current version, such as a revised document that replaces its earlier draft.
